items.title: My favourite segment is the desert: Kalyan Varma on his documentary Wild Tamil Nadu
items.summary: Wild Tamil Nadu , an hour-long documentary directed by Kalyan Varma, is a love story of sorts, narrated with nuance and put together with deep respect for the creatures filmed. A tribute to Tamil Nadu and its unique landscape as referenced in Sangam literature — Kurunji (the mountains), Mullai (forests), Marutam (crop land and rivers), Neidhal (seashore) and Paalai (desert), it is now playing in select PVR screens. Kalyan, who earlier co-directed Wild Karnataka , is an award-winning documentary filmmaker. What makes Wild Tamil Nadu fascinating is how much you take back from it. Creatures, some big but many small, shine under the spotlight. The documentary is produced by Arathi Krishna of Sundaram Fasteners. Director Kalyan Varma Music by Ricky Kej, which primarily features Indian sounds, lifts the experience, while editor Akhilesh Thambe manages to compress hours of footage into a memorable, even action-packed, 60 minutes. Actor Arvind Swami lends his rich voice for both the Tamil and English versions. In an interview with TNM, director Kalyan speaks of what went into the making of the documentary, how he likes to showcase wildlife and some of the creative choices exercised. Below
